passage: You look sad that your friends are all online tonight, beta. Let me tell you about when I was eleven. I'm Anjali, your aunt. My friends, Joseph and the others, had started playing one online game every evening, and if I didn't join I felt lonely, like a chair nobody sat in. So I joined, for hours. Afterwards my head felt heavy and I was grumpy with everyone at home. I noticed that. So one Sunday I said, "Joseph, come play tag outside, just for an hour." He grumbled, but he came, and two others followed. We were sweaty and loud, and I felt lighter. We still played online sometimes, but not every evening.

qa.q: Who did Anjali ask to come and play tag outside?
qa.a: She asked Joseph to come and play tag outside.

qa.q: How did Anjali feel when she was not part of the online game?
qa.a: Lonely, like a chair nobody sat in.

qa.q: What did Anjali try instead of joining every evening?
qa.a: She noticed how she felt after long screen time and invited her friends to play outside.

qa.q: How might Joseph have seen Anjali's invitation to play tag?
qa.a: He grumbled at first, so he may have been reluctant, but he came, which suggests he was willing to be asked.

grounding: A child feels lonely when friends prefer online play, notices how long screen time leaves her feeling, and invites them outside.

passage:
In the hostel common room, evening free hour meant one thing now: six boys on their phones in a silent row, playing the same online battle game. Saurabh sat with them. If he didn't, he was alone.
After an hour his eyes stung, and he felt cranky and strangely flat. He had barely spoken a word to anyone.
Through the window he saw Reena from the girls' block setting out the rounders bats on the field.
Saurabh stood up. "Who's coming for rounders? Reena's team needs players."
Nobody looked up. Then Dev lowered his phone. "Okay. One game."
One game turned into four. Saurabh walked back flushed and laughing. Tomorrow, he decided, he would ask again, and notice how he felt after each.

qa.q: What was Reena setting out on the field?
How did Saurabh feel after an hour of playing in the common room?
qa.a: Cranky and flat, with stinging eyes, even though he was sitting with friends.

qa.q: What did Saurabh try, and what could he keep doing?
qa.a: He invited the others to rounders; he can keep inviting them and notice how he feels after screens compared with play.

qa.q: How might Dev have felt after the four games?
qa.a: Dev was probably glad he lowered his phone, since one game turned into four.

grounding: A boy who feels lonely unless he joins his friends' online games invites them outside and notices how long screen time leaves him feeling.

passage:
Saturday: At Charu's house, Charu and two other friends played the same online game, headphones on, all afternoon. Sabina sat beside them with her own tablet. By evening her head felt heavy, and she realised nobody had actually talked to her.
Monday: After school Sabina texted Charu, "Skipping on my terrace? I have the long rope 😊". Charu wrote back, "Maybe, after my match." She never came. Sabina skipped alone, counting out loud, and felt left behind.
Wednesday: Sabina asked again, this time in person. "Just half an hour. I miss you." Charu looked surprised, then pulled off her headphones. On the terrace they reached two hundred skips together, gasping with laughter. Walking home, Sabina noticed her head felt light, not heavy.

qa.q: How many skips did the girls reach together?
How did Sabina feel on Monday when Charu never came?
What did Sabina do differently on Wednesday that worked?
qa.a: She asked in person and said she missed Charu, instead of only texting.

qa.q: How might Charu have seen Sabina's "I miss you"?
qa.a: Charu was surprised, perhaps not knowing Sabina felt left out, and it made her take off her headphones.

grounding: A girl whose friend only wants to play online feels lonely, invites her to play outside and notices how she feels after screens.
